blocks.description: Languages, name, search, header, footer and twelve feature switches live on one screen. Save once, and every connected application takes the change in seconds, without a rebuild.

blocks.text: On this element’s pages, in one of eight groups, and saves.
In APP-CONFIG and PLATFORM-CONFIG, written as a patch, never overwritten.
Every subscribed application gets it the moment you save and takes the new settings itself.
The application applies them over its own defaults, and visitors see the change after reloading.
In a single project every element takes its settings from here; in an app factory a new element keeps its own.

blocks.title: On, asleep only when memory is short

blocks.text: The element starts with the node. With less than 0.5 GB of free memory the node may put it to sleep; the first call or a calendar entry wakes it in seconds, and above 1 GB free it comes back by itself.

blocks.text: This page is a working tool as well as a description: languages, the title, search, the header, the footer and twelve switches change on this element's pages, and every connected application follows within seconds, with no rebuild.
Only the architect can change them, after signing in. Visitors never see these pages.
Each one turns a feature of every connected application on or off:

blocks.text: CONFIG is an addition, not a foundation. An application that connects over MCP gets one place where all its settings change; only the architect changes them, after signing in, and applications read them with the node’s key.

blocks.title: Your own builder comes with it

blocks.text: Every element of the node comes with its own Claude Code agent and can get its own Telegram bot. When something in this element should change, write to its bot from your phone, and the agent updates the logic or the design.
The agent works only in its element's folder and never reads the whole node, so each change costs fewer tokens. Your Claude Code subscription pays for it.

items: The element's bot is connected in the core, on its «Telegram» page.
The agent returns a commit; you look at it in «Preview» and accept it or turn it down.
At the computer, the agent's terminal is in the core, in this element's «Build».

blocks.text: Built by Fractera for the [Lagrix](https://lagrix.dev) protocol and for any web2 project with more than one application. MIT license, the code is at [github.com/Fractera/fractera-config-starter](https://github.com/Fractera/fractera-config-starter).

items.q: Does an application need CONFIG to run?
items.a: No. Each application keeps its own settings and works without it; CONFIG gives one place to change them all.

items.q: How fast does a change arrive?
items.a: On save every subscribed application gets a signal and takes the new settings; visitors see them after a reload.
A new element keeps settings of its own; in a single project every element takes them from here.
